data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The night-time UHI gap is primarily driven by stored sensible heat in high thermal mass materials (asphalt, masonry) that is released after sunset, and the gap scales with the city's impervious surface fraction and building density.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If rural and urban surfaces share identical thermal admittance and heat capacity, the stored heat differential vanishes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If sustained high winds mix the urban boundary layer thoroughly with rural air, the localized sensible heat release is dissipated before forming a temperature gap.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Urban materials have high heat capacity and thermal mass, absorbing intense daytime solar radiation.
